title: A pure-tensor counterexample to a literal analytic-rank tensorization inequality
oneLine: A side-two pure trilinear tensor refutes one literal, unnormalised analytic-rank tensorization comparator, while the powered-identity diagonal ratio remains exactly (k/n)^m.
abstract: An archived AIM problem-list page displays a tensorization inequality for analytic rank or partition rank. Under standard base-p analytic rank and fixed-order Kronecker powers, its literal, unnormalised analytic-rank instantiation is false. Over F2, a side-two pure trilinear tensor has analytic rank a=log_2(4/3), the identity has rank 2a, and every Kronecker power of the pure tensor still has rank a. Since 2a<1, the proposed scalar bound (2ac)^m tends to zero for every fixed 0<c<1. On diagonal tensors, comparison with the powered identity instead gives the exact ratio (k/n)^m. The diagonal formula and normalization principle are known; the possible contribution is only their application to this literal comparator. The release does not refute a normalized or powered-identity formulation, determine the source's intended meaning, or settle partition rank. Exact derivation, finite producer replay, seven negative controls, review repair, public CI and byte-matched GitHub and Zenodo assets support the candidate; independent reproduction, formal verification, external specialist review, editorial peer review, novelty and priority remain unestablished.
narration: This result begins with one small but decisive distinction. An archived AIM problem-list page displays a tensorization bound using the analytic rank of the identity, raised as a scalar to the m-th power. Read literally and without normalization, that analytic-rank statement is false. Work over the field with two elements, at tensor order three and side length two. A pure diagonal tensor has analytic rank a, where a is log base two of four thirds. The two-coordinate identity has analytic rank two a. But every fixed-order Kronecker power of the pure tensor still has just one active diagonal coordinate, so its analytic rank remains a. The exact inequality sixteen ninths is less than two shows that two a is below one. Therefore, for every fixed c below one, the proposed right-hand side, two a c to the m, tends to zero and eventually falls below a. There is also a clean repair diagnostic. If the denominator is the analytic rank of the powered identity, then on every diagonal tensor the ratio is exactly k over n to the m. The release does not claim that this powered formulation is the uniquely intended one. It does not settle partition rank, historical intention, novelty, or priority. Python and JavaScript replay, direct small coefficient enumeration, seven negative controls, and public Linux CI support the arithmetic and finite bridges. They are producer-side checks, not independent reconstruction or peer review. This synthetic-voice briefing is a communication aid, not additional mathematical evidence.

problem.name: AIM Problem 1.3: Polynomial method via tensorizing

keyResults: Under base-p analytic rank and fixed-order Kronecker powers, the literal unnormalised analytic-rank instantiation of the archived comparator is false.
Over F2 at order three and side length two, a pure tensor has analytic rank a=log_2(4/3), the identity has rank 2a, and every positive Kronecker power of the pure tensor has rank a.
The exact inequality 16/9<2 gives 2a<1, so the proposed scalar right-hand side (2ac)^m tends to zero for every fixed 0<c<1.
For a k-supported diagonal tensor in side length n, comparison with the powered identity gives the exact ratio (k/n)^m.
evidence: A five-page DOI-bearing manuscript and aligned Markdown; a self-contained exact proof; a checksum-bound archived source extract; dependency-free Python normal and optimized replay; same-producer JavaScript reimplementation; direct coefficient evaluation over 64 assignments at m=1 and 4,096 assignments at m=2; seven semantic negative controls; claim, convention, source, citation and bounded novelty audits; a supplied Major Revision review and full response matrix; one producer-coordinated five-role internal editorial gate; a 51-file manifested ZIP; a five-job public GitHub Actions replay and PDF rebuild; and exact GitHub and Zenodo asset readback. These establish public availability, integrity, producer replay and the stated conditional theorem—not historical intention, partition-rank resolution, independent reproduction, formal verification, authenticated external specialist review, editorial peer review, novelty, priority or impact.
statusDetail: Anonymous, unrefereed conditional counterexample candidate at PASS_WITH_NOTES after actioning a supplied Major Revision report and completing a producer-coordinated five-role internal editorial gate. Reviewer identity, credentials and unaffiliated status were not authenticated. The diagonal bias formula and normalization principle are known; no first-discovery or priority claim is made.
